Serving Heavy Content

~25 MB of 1080p/720p clips served straight out of the embedded resource bundle. The stage above is the real-world case — a hover-driven video background — and the checks below assert the embedded scheme answers HTTP byte-range requests (200 / 206 / 416).

Waiting for the hover stress run…
CheckResultDetail

Before this fix, the embedded scheme served resources through a whole-file-copy, no-range provider, so WKWebView / WebView2 media loaders range-thrashed (hundreds of requests, each re-materialising the file) and <video> failed with “An error occurred trying to load the resource.” Now embedded resources go through the streaming provider: each range copies only the bytes asked for, straight from static memory.

The stage is also a lesson for the page side. A hover background that swaps src on one element — or lets the element remount — re-downloads the clip on every hover and shows a frozen first frame, or nothing, however good the range support is. One element per clip, created once, is what makes it smooth: hover only toggles opacity and play/pause.
